q: 1. The formula, F = R - K(1.8 T + 32), for obtaining the annual run-off is known as .............
explain: Khosla's formula is a widely used empirical relationship in India for calculating run-off based on temperature and rainfall.

q: 2. The amount of water collected in a reservoir is divided into three portions and the order of their existence from bottom to the top is .............
options: useful storage, surcharge storage, dead storage
useful storage, dead storage, surcharge storage
dead storage, useful storage, surcharge storage
explain: Dead storage is at the bottom (cannot be drawn), followed by useful storage, and surcharge storage is the volume above the full reservoir level.

q: 3. The slow sand filters should be cleaned if the loss of head becomes more than .............
explain: When the head loss reaches approximately 0.7 to 1.2 meters (roughly 70% to 80% of the sand bed depth), the filter is considered 'clogged' and requires scraping.

q: 4. A sluice valve, in water distribution system, is used to .............
options: protect the pipe against negative pressure
regulate the flow of water through the pipe
prevent water of flow back in the opposite direction
explain: Sluice valves (Gate valves) are used to isolate sections of the network or regulate the flow by opening/closing the pipe path.

q: 5. A reflux valve, in water distribution system is used to .............
options: protect the pipe against negative pressure
regulate the flow of water through the pipe
prevent water of flow back in the opposite direction
explain: A Reflux valve allows water to flow in one direction only, preventing backflow into pumps or reservoirs.

q: 6. A reflux valve is also known as .............
explain: Check valve and non-return valve are common alternative names for a reflux valve.

q: 7. A scour valve, in a water distribution system, is provided at .............
explain: Scour valves (Blow-off valves) are placed at low points to drain the pipe and remove accumulated silt/sediment.

q: 8. If the level of sources of water is higher than that of the place of consumption, the system adopted for supplying water is .............
explain: A gravity system uses the natural elevation difference to move water without the need for mechanical pumps.

q: 9. A pressure relief valve is provided to
options: the back flow, when the pump is stopped
prevent the increase of pressure after certain safe limit
explain: Pressure relief valves are safety devices designed to open and release fluid when the pressure exceeds a predefined limit, protecting the pipe from bursting.

q: 10. A valve which allows the water to flow in one direction but prevents its flows in the reverse direction, is known as
explain: Reflux valves (check valves) are automatic valves that permit flow in only one direction and close automatically to prevent backflow.

q: 11. The suitable layout of a distribution system for well-planned cities is
explain: The ring (circular) system is ideal for well-planned cities where the main pipe follows the periphery, ensuring constant pressure and supply from two directions.

q: 12. Design period mainly depends on ...........
options: percentage interest at which the loan is taken
capacity of the municipality to repay
explain: The design period (how long the project should last) is chosen based on how fast the population is growing. Rapid growth requires shorter design periods to avoid obsolescence.

q: 13. Combined pumping and gravity flow system is best suited, where ............
options: the city is in plains and source is fairly elevated
the city had a gentle slope and source is elevated
the city is on steep slopes and source is below
explain: A combined system (pumping to a reservoir, then gravity to consumers) is versatile and can be adapted to almost any topographical layout.

q: 14. A disadvantage of combined pumping and gravity flow is that ............
options: it needs pumping round the clock
adequate pressure may not exist in pipes
we may not get enough water to fight fire
explain: The main drawback is the high capital cost and space requirement for constructing elevated storage reservoirs (Overhead Tanks).

q: 15. An advantage of intermittent system of supply of water is ............
options: supply is assured during a fire accident
repairs can be carried out during non-supply hours
explain: In an intermittent system, water is only supplied for a few hours. This allows maintenance crews to perform repairs on pipes during the 'off' hours without wasting water.

q: 16. A major disadvantage of intermittent system of supply of water is ............
options: infiltration of impurities may occur through leaky joints
explain: When the water supply is off, the pressure in the pipes drops. This creates a vacuum that can suck in contaminated groundwater through leaks in the joints.

q: 17. Intermittent system is more popular in Nepal because ............
options: supply hours can be staggered for different zones of different elevations
less quantity of water shall be sufficient
it is highly economical in the long run
explain: Due to the hilly topography and limited water resources, supply is staggered to ensure different zones receive water at specific scheduled times.

q: 18. The purpose of stand pipe is that it ............
options: is of great help in intermittent supply system
explain: Standpipes act as surge tanks or small reservoirs that help maintain and boost hydraulic pressure in the distribution network.

q: 19. Losses in distribution system are due to ............
options: poor quality of pipes and fitting
dead end system of net work of pipes
explain: Physical losses (leaks) are primarily caused by corroded or poor-quality pipe materials and faulty joint fittings.

q: 20. The only advantage of dead end system is ............
options: it had more number of dead ends
blow of values empty stagnant pocket of water
explain: The dead-end (tree) system requires the least amount of total pipe length, making it the cheapest to install initially.

q: 21. Grid iron system is best suited to ............
options: planned city on a gentle slope
explain: The Grid Iron system follows a rectangular pattern, which is perfectly suited for planned cities with a systematic road network.

q: 22. The valve that is most commonly provided on rising mains is ............
explain: Reflux valves (check valves) are placed on rising mains to prevent the backflow of water to the pump when it stops.
